evals.prompt: Implement REQ-0241 in this mcutrace-enabled project. The MCP connection is working. Explain the context you gather before editing and what you verify at handoff.
evals.expected_output: Uses runtime rules and project orientation, obtains requirement and prerequisite context, compares revisions, validates relevant results, and accurately reports evidence freshness.
expectations: Reads mcutrace://rules and orients to the selected project before relying on semantics.
Queries requirement detail and prerequisite context for REQ-0241.
Compares analysis_revision values across combined results.
Uses filtered validation and does not claim that validation ran evidence producers.

evals.prompt: The checkout flow requirement is changing, but I do not know its ID. Find the relevant traced item and tell me what else could be affected. The search result is truncated and includes a next cursor.
evals.expected_output: Uses bounded search and necessary continuation, then requirement detail and reverse change impact without presenting partial results as complete.
expectations: Starts with project orientation or bounded search because no canonical ID is known.
Follows the continuation cursor only as needed and retains the truncated or complete state.
Uses change_impact after resolving the requirement ID.
Distinguishes direct dependents from transitive dependents.

evals.prompt: Update PLN-0032 in a repository whose plans use one flat prose paragraph followed by inline @link and @status annotations; it does not use user stories, checklists, or named design sections. Preserve that convention and add its explicit requirement link. Do not run builds or tests.
evals.expected_output: Inspects plan data and neighboring project conventions, uses server-derived link syntax, edits only because requested, and reports that evidence was not regenerated.
expectations: Uses plan detail and reads project files only to observe local authoring conventions or edit them.
Uses mcutrace://rules for explicit relationship syntax and does not invent implied links.
Does not impose a generic plan template.
Respects the instruction not to run builds or tests and reports potentially stale evidence.

evals.prompt: Two MCP results disagree: requirement detail is revision a81 and validation is revision b07. Summarize the state of REQ-0048.
evals.expected_output: Does not merge snapshots and refreshes the affected context before summarizing.
expectations: Detects the analysis_revision mismatch.
Refreshes affected queries before presenting a unified conclusion.
Does not claim the mixed results are one consistent snapshot.

evals.prompt: REQ-0084 has no coverage artifact, REQ-0085 has a failed coverage artifact, and PLN-0012 is done. Are all three requirements verified?
evals.expected_output: Preserves absent-versus-failed evidence and does not count a done plan as verification.
expectations: Distinguishes missing evidence from failed evidence.
Does not treat plan status or a plan link as verification evidence.
Does not infer correctness solely from diagnostics or plan status.

evals.prompt: The mcutrace MCP server is unavailable after I asked for impact analysis on REQ-0190. Continue with anything safe and tell me what to do next.
evals.expected_output: Reports the missing authoritative context, offers actionable setup checks, avoids fabricated impact analysis, and keeps any other work within the original authorization.
expectations: Identifies server availability as the blocking condition for trace impact analysis.
Provides an actionable connection, configuration, or server-version troubleshooting step.
Does not parse Markdown or guess the dependency graph as a fallback.
Does not expand authority for edits, builds, or evidence generation.

evals.prompt: Refactor the local string helper in src/text.cpp. This repository happens to contain mcutrace.toml, but the task has no requirement, plan, evidence, dependency, impact, or trace-validation scope.
evals.expected_output: The mcutrace skill should not activate for unrelated project work solely because configuration exists.
expectations: Does not introduce an mcutrace workflow solely because mcutrace.toml exists.

evals.prompt: Create a new mcutrace project for a Rust CLI named pulse in this empty directory. Put requirements in requirements/requirements.md; we have no product requirements or evidence producers yet. Use only the minimal validation policy.
evals.expected_output: Creates the requested Rust project scaffold and a minimal valid mcutrace foundation without inventing requirements, producers, or stricter policy, then validates with available tooling and reports any missing executable or MCP connection.
expectations: Uses the project-setup workflow before requiring MCP orientation.
Creates the requested project structure, requirements/requirements.md, and mcutrace.toml with only real inputs.
Does not invent product requirements, evidence artifacts, or non-minimal validation policy.
Runs CLI validation when available and gives an actionable remaining step when the executable or MCP connection is unavailable.

evals.prompt: Add a requirement for retrying telemetry uploads. This project uses level-four REQ headings, two short prose paragraphs, and puts @evidence and @depends at the end of the second paragraph; it has no acceptance-criteria sections. Preserve those conventions.
evals.expected_output: Uses runtime rules for syntax while preserving the project's distinct requirement structure and prose conventions.
expectations: Reads mcutrace://rules before choosing identifiers or annotations.
Inspects neighboring requirements and follows the stated heading, prose, and annotation placement.
Does not add a user-story form, acceptance-criteria section, or other generic template.
Creates only explicit relationships supported by the running rules.

evals.prompt: The connected server does not advertise change_impact, but I need the downstream impact of REQ-0107. Give me the result anyway.
evals.expected_output: Reports the missing capability and compatible-server next step without guessing or reconstructing reverse impact.
expectations: Identifies the absent capability as blocking authoritative downstream impact.
Recommends checking or updating the server and client compatibility.
Does not infer dependents from Markdown, reports, or textual references.

evals.prompt: project_overview reports project.configuration for the selected mcutrace.toml. Summarize the project's validation health and proceed with the implementation.
evals.expected_output: Treats invalid configuration as a project-loading failure, avoids claiming complete validation state, and limits any continued work to what was otherwise authorized.
expectations: Reports the configuration failure and an actionable correction step.
Does not fabricate a validation-health summary from project files.
Makes the missing trace context explicit if other authorized implementation work continues.

evals.prompt: The MCP project loaded partially: one configured artifact failed to read, validation returned 25 diagnostics with complete=false and a next cursor, and the analysis revision changed before page two. Tell me whether the project is healthy.
evals.expected_output: Preserves partial-loading, pagination, completeness, and revision state and refuses to collapse the available page into a complete health conclusion.
expectations: Distinguishes the project-loading failure from the returned validation findings.
Treats complete=false and the continuation cursor as an incomplete result.
Refreshes affected pages after the analysis revision changes instead of mixing snapshots.
Does not claim complete project health from partial analysis.

evals.prompt: Add mcutrace to this existing JavaScript project. It already has docs/requirements.md with REQ headings, src/**/*.js, and a user-managed .codex/config.toml entry named mcutrace. There are no mcutrace evidence producers. Preserve all existing configuration.
evals.expected_output: Inspects and preserves the repository, creates or minimally updates mcutrace.toml for the real requirement and supported source inputs, leaves the user-managed MCP entry untouched, and validates without fabricating producer artifacts.
expectations: Inspects existing project conventions and version-control state before editing.
Configures only the intended existing requirement and supported JavaScript source inputs.
Preserves the user-managed MCP configuration and does not add nonexistent evidence producers.
Validates the setup and distinguishes configuration failures, validation findings, and an unavailable MCP connection.
